title: Sine-Gordon Model with Bosonic Tensor Networks: Continuum Matching and Soliton Scattering
authors: Florian Hechenberger, Tommaso Rainaldi, Felix Ringer
abstract: We use bosonic tensor networks to connect the lattice sine-Gordon model in the Hamiltonian formulation quantitatively to its continuum theory. Matching the lattice vertex operator to its conformal normalization at the free-boson ultraviolet fixed point yields the exact relation between the bare lattice coupling and the renormalized continuum mass parameter. The soliton mass then approaches Zamolodchikov's exact continuum prediction throughout the studied parameter range, without adjustable parameters. Using uniform matrix product states and a quasiparticle ansatz, we also recover the relativistic soliton dispersion and the two lightest breather masses at the percent level. We simulate real-time collisions of Gaussian soliton-antisoliton wave packets near a reflectionless point and extract the Wigner spatial displacement. We compare this displacement with the exact continuum prediction obtained from the momentum derivative of the transmission phase, recovering its characteristic rapidity dependence. Our bosonic simulations provide a foundation for nonintegrable extensions, offer lessons for renormalization in other Hamiltonian lattice field theories, including gauge theories, and provide benchmarks for continuous-variable quantum simulations.
summary: This paper uses bosonic tensor networks to bridge the gap between the lattice Sine-Gordon model and its continuum limit. By matching lattice couplings to continuum normalization, the authors accurately predict key physical quantities like soliton masses and scattering dynamics. This work establishes a robust numerical framework for studying renormalization and dynamics in quantum field theories.
main_problem: The paper aims to quantitatively connect the lattice Sine-Gordon model to its continuum theory and study the dynamics of soliton scattering.
main_result: The bosonic simulations successfully recover the exact continuum predictions for the soliton mass, breather masses, and the characteristic rapidity dependence of the Wigner spatial displacement during collisions.
method: The study employs bosonic tensor networks (MPS) for time evolution and uses continuum matching techniques by comparing lattice vertex operators to conformal field theory normalization.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Sine-Gordon model in 1+1 dimensions, described by a Hamiltonian involving a cosine potential. The analysis uses lattice discretization and bosonic tensor networks to simulate quantum dynamics.
key_observables: Soliton mass ($M_{sol}$), breather masses, and the Wigner spatial displacement ($\Delta x$) during soliton-antisoliton scattering.
important_parameters: The bare lattice coupling, the renormalized continuum mass parameter, and the parameter $ eta^2/(8\pi)$ governing the model's flow.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the ability to perform continuum matching at the free-boson UV fixed point and assumes the validity of the variational ansatz for state construction.
figures_summary: Figures compare the measured antisymmetric displacement during scattering against theoretical predictions derived from momentum eigenstates and wave packet averages, showing good agreement.
paper_structure: The work proceeds by first establishing the continuum matching procedure, then using tensor networks to simulate the time evolution of localized excitations (solitons) and finally analyzing the scattering dynamics by measuring the Wigner displacement.
why_interesting: The use of bosonic tensor networks to simulate integrable field theories like Sine-Gordon provides a powerful, non-perturbative benchmark for quantum simulation techniques applicable to other complex Hamiltonian lattice field theories.
